title: Inherent Defects and Behavior of ALD-grown ZnO Thin Films During Electron Irradiation
content: Zinc oxide (ZnO) is a promising material for space-grade microelectronics due to its exceptional resistance to high-energy radiation [1]. This stability makes ZnO less susceptible to single-event upsets (SEUs), which occur when ionizing radiation deposits enough energy to flip a bit in a digital circuit, leading to data corruption or malfunctions. As a result, ZnO outperforms traditional silicon semiconductors in extreme, space-like environments.
